name: NJ-11
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+5 district sits in a strongly favorable national environment for Democrats this cycle
Incumbent Mejia holds a roughly 2-to-1 fundraising edge and faces no outside opposition spending
Polymarket prices the Democrat near 95 percent, consistent with fundamentals
No public polls or expert ratings, keeping uncertainty elevated
model.rationale: A five-point Democratic district, a favorable national environment, and Mejia's clear fundraising advantage over Hathaway all point the same direction, and prediction markets agree at about 95 percent Democratic. With no polling or contrary evidence, the fundamentals-based estimate of a double-digit Democratic margin stands.
model.watch: Late Republican outside spending, a first-ever poll showing a single-digit race, or signs of first-term incumbent underperformance could tighten the outlook.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
New Jersey's 11th District leans Democratic by five points, and the broader political environment this year favors Democrats nationwide. Incumbent Analilia Mejia has raised about $2.1 million to Republican Joe Hathaway's $807,000, and neither side is facing outside opposition spending. No independent public polls of the general election are available, so the picture rests on district fundamentals, money, and the national climate.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 95 percent, and race raters have paid the contest little attention, consistent with a seat the party holds comfortably. Hathaway has raised a credible sum for a challenger but ends the period with little cash, and an independent candidate on the ballot reports no fundraising. Everything points to a comfortable Democratic win; the main uncertainty is simply the absence of polling data.
